# Narrow source-parser corpus

The expected JSON was transcribed independently before parser implementation from
the reviewed design and checked against the four official archives with the web
reader on 2026-10-29. It is not generated by production parsing.

The two `frb-*.html` fixtures contain only the release date and summary numerical
table extracted from actual publisher HTML obtained on 2026-10-29. The parent
`data-table-1` wrapper was reconstructed to preserve the table's seasonal-unit
association. Their full original acquisition records are in the ignored local
`var/source-review` directory; `provenance.json` preserves original raw and fixture
hashes. These fixtures do not include logos, photographs, scripts or navigation.

The two `bls-*-modeled.html` fixtures are **hand-authored structural examples**.
The publisher denied the direct Python requests with HTTP403. The web reader
confirmed the values, release header and adjacent SA/NSA column semantics, but did
not deliver original HTML bytes to this importer. The deliberately poisoned
unadjusted values are synthetic. These tests establish parser behavior for the
modeled structure, not successful real BLS acquisition or real BLS HTML parsing.
Never import these modeled fixtures into the real archive collection.

Attribution: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation, 2024-02-02 and
2024-03-08, Table B-1; Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, G.17,
2024-02-15 and 2024-03-15, Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization: Summary.

The project retains only the attributed publisher-produced numerical material described in `data/README.md`. Runtime use restrictions are separate from the software license; see `docs/SOURCE-CONTRACT.md`.
